episodes.161212: Showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall ahead of an approaching cold front.
episodes.161216: Scattered showers and storms developed in a warm, humid airmass with moderate CAPE and shear ahead of an approaching cold front on September 15, 2021. One particularly strong storm produced widespread wind damage in Centre County, with isolated reports of wind damage elsewhere.  Another storm brought flash flooding to Sullivan County near LaPorte.
episodes.161220: Ample instability combined with an approaching cold front to produce a line of showers and thunderstorms across central Indiana by the late afternoon of the 14th. The storms progressed eastward through the evening, some with strong winds and heavy rain ... while the most intense cells produced marginally severe winds and small hail.
episodes.161237: A cold front moved across a moderately unstable air mass across central and southern VT during the afternoon of September 15th. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the southern Champlain Valley and Upper Hudson Valley of New York and moved into central and southern VT. Some of these storms intensified across VT delivering isolated to scattered wind damage to trees and utility lines.
episodes.161238: A potent warm front with some elevated convection produced isolated to scattered thunderstorms across northern NY during the early morning hours of September 15th. One such storm in Brushton briefly produced a wind gust that knocked a tree onto some power lines.
episodes.161291: While most of northern and central New Mexico was under the influence of a strong high pressure system with hot and dry conditions, a backdoor cold front entering northeast New Mexico did allow for a few thunderstorms on September 14, 2021. An increase in low-level moisture in addition to favorable upslope flow along the northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains and Johnson and Bartlett Mesas allowed for the development of afternoon and evening thunderstorms. Favorable wind shear also allowed for the brief organization of these thunderstorms as they tracked southeast across the northeast plains. A thunderstorm near Folsom in northern Union County did briefly become severe when it produced high winds in the area.
episodes.161435: The sea breeze along with a weak shortwave helped produce scattered thunderstorms in a high moisture environment leading to minor urban flash flooding.
episodes.161452: A few thunderstorms became severe producing damaging wind gusts over western and north-central Maryland during the afternoon, as well as over northeastern Maryland during the evening.
episodes.161694: As a surface trough passed north of the islands, it triggered heavy showers over portions of the state.  The downpours produced ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  There were no reports of significant property damage or injuries.
episodes.162067: Rain from the remnants of Hurricane Nicholas affected portions of southern Mississippi. Amounts up to 5 inches fell, which resulted in some flooding across the area.
episodes.162244: Weak fair weather waterspout spotted off eastern Brunswick County coast.
episodes.162569: Rainfall accumulation over the period combined with previously saturated soils and elevated river levels produce flooding with damage to homes and neighborhoods.
episodes.162617: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 15th across northeastern Oklahoma, along a weak stationary frontal boundary. The air mass across the region had become moderately unstable during the afternoon, but wind shear was very weak. As a result, storms that developed were short-lived. The strongest thunderstorms produced brief, damaging wind gusts.
episodes.162945: A passing cold front triggered many storms across Central New York. An unstable environment provided support for a few storms to become severe. Damaging wind gusts were the main hazard, but one storm was able to produce large hail as well.
episodes.162947: A passing cold front triggered many storms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. An unstable environment provided support for a couple storms to become severe. Damaging wind gusts were the main hazard.
episodes.162966: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms impacted southeast Michigan on the afternoon of September 14, 2021 as a cold front tracked across the region.
episodes.162974: Scattered thunderstorms occurred in association with a surface trough extending northward from Tropical Depression Nicholas, which was located near the Louisiana coast. Locally very heavy rain caused minor flooding.
episodes.162996: Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Hurricane Nicholas moved across the marine area and produced strong, gusty winds.
episodes.163013: A nearly-stationary front was draped in vicinity of the major axis of Lake Erie during the early evening of September 12th through the wee hours of the 13th as one low drifted northeastward over western Kansas and another remained nearly-stationary in vicinity of Labrador. A bow echo moved east-southeastward across central and eastern Lake Erie during the evening of the 12th and produced a couple of gale-force peak wind gusts along the Erie County, PA lakeshore during the 10 PM EST hour. The bow echo encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.    ||The front then wavered in vicinity of Lake Erie through the late evening of the 13th as the Kansas low moved toward Iowa and consolidated with another low moving from western Montana. Simultaneously, the Canadian low drifted eastward and offshore Labrador. The front then moved northeastward from Lake Erie as a warm front during the morning of the 14th and allowed the warm sector to overspread all of Lake Erie through the early evening as the consolidated low moved from Iowa toward central Ontario. The low then moved farther northeastward to northern Quebec by the early morning of the 15th, which is when the trailing cold front began to move eastward across the western basin of Lake Erie. ||A squall line outpaced the cold front and moved generally eastward across Lake Erie during the late evening of the 14th. This line of showers and thunderstorms produced gale-force peak wind gusts along the northern Ohio shore. The showers and storms encountered moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.
episodes.163015: Northern Ohio resided in the warm sector during the evening of the 14th as a low moved northeastward across central Ontario and central Quebec. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front approached northwest Ohio from southeast Lower Michigan and northern Indiana.|A squall line outpaced the cold front and moved generally eastward across northwest Ohio during the late evening of the 14th. This line of showers and thunderstorms produced one measured severe wind gust and isolated straight-line wind damage. The showers and storms encountered moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.
episodes.163020: Ahead of a southeast moving cold front, a west to east oriented band of heavy precipitation formed across central Kentucky along a boundary remaining from precipitation from the previous night. As rain continued along this boundary, areas of flash flooding occurred in Nelson County.||Later in the day, a report of flooding was received from Simpson County as the cold front worked its way through south central Kentucky.
episodes.163052: A line of showers and thunderstorms resulted in widespread severe weather and flash flooding over eastern New York on Wednesday September 15, 2021.
episodes.163166: A cold front moved through during the afternoon and evening with a line of thunderstorms. Most storms were sub-severe, but several produced small hail, and a few had damaging wind gusts.
episodes.163181: A line of showers and thunderstorms resulted in severe weather damage over southern Vermont on Wednesday September 15, 2021.
episodes.163187: Scattered thunderstorms, some strong to severe, occurred over the plains. The strongest storms developed around mid afternoon through mid evening, and produced hail up to 1 to 1.25 inches and wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.163277: Heavy rainfall from showers and thunderstorm led to isolated instances of flash flooding in Washington County.
episodes.163321: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the morning hours on September 15th. There was one isolated flooding report in Perry County.
episodes.163376: Thunderstorms moving through Lake St. Clair produced wind gusts up to 45 knots.
episodes.163378: A thunderstorm moving into Lake Erie produced a wind gust around 40 knots.
episodes.163382: A couple of storms developed on the 14th and 15th producing minimal severe weather across the area.
episodes.163404: Hurricane Nicholas moved into the central Texas coast early on the 14th. The remnants of the system moved into Louisiana the late on the 14th then drifted around the state causing flooding.
episodes.163434: Tropical Storm Nicholas made landfall on the Texas coast south of Houston early Tuesday morning on September 14th. Over the next 24 hours, the weakening storm slowly tracked east-northeast along the coastline, reaching the LA/TX border Wednesday morning. During the 14th and 15th, outer bands of Nicholas expanded east across southeast Louisiana. The persistent rain from those banding features produced areas of flash flooding.
episodes.163435: Tropical Storm Nicholas made landfall on the Texas coast south of Houston early Tuesday morning on September 14th. Over the next 24 hours, the weakening storm slowly tracked east-northeast along the coastline, reaching the LA/TX border Wednesday morning. During the 14th and 15th, outer bands of Nicholas expanded east across coastal waters southeast of Louisiana and Mississippi. Stronger cells within those bands produced severe winds.
episodes.163437: Tropical Storm Nicholas made landfall on the Texas coast south of Houston early Tuesday morning on September 14th. Over the next 24 hours, the weakening storm slowly tracked east-northeast along the coastline, reaching the LA/TX border Wednesday morning. During the 14th and 15th, outer bands of Nicholas expanded east across coastal Mississippi. The persistent rain from those banding features produced areas of flash flooding.
episodes.163460: Ahead of a cold front, a broken line of thunderstorms formed on Tuesday evening from southern Ontario to northern Ohio. Eventually these storm storms moved east across our area, resulting in general 40 to 50 mph winds on Lake Erie.
episodes.163461: Ahead of a cold front, a broken line of thunderstorms formed on Tuesday evening from southern Ontario to northern Ohio. Eventually these storm storms moved east across our area, resulting in wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph Lake Erie, 30 to 40 mph on Lake Ontario, and nearly 50 mph along the St. Lawrence River.
episodes.163481: Deep tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Nicholas overspread the area and led to the development of bands of very heavy rainfall. The slow motion of these bands produced copious amounts of rain which led to flash flooding across portions of southwest Alabama.
episodes.163522: A late season severe weather outbreak occurred across New Hampshire as a cold front swept across the state during the afternoon peak heating.  A very moist and unstable airmass was in place across the region with highs reaching 80 degrees and dewpoints into the 60s.  This allowed for sufficient CAPE values to support damaging winds gusts and large hail as the cold front moved across the state.
episodes.163523: A late season severe weather outbreak occurred across Maine as a cold front swept across the state during the afternoon peak heating.  A very moist and unstable airmass was in place across the region with highs reaching 80 degrees and dewpoints into the 60s.  This allowed for sufficient CAPE values to support damaging winds gusts and large hail as the cold front moved across the state.
episodes.163533: Deep tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Nicholas overspread the area and led to the development of bands of very heavy rainfall. The slow motion of these bands produced copious amounts of rain which led to flash flooding across portions of northwest Florida.
episodes.163540: A strong occluded low pressure system was located in southeast Canada, resulting in scattered severe weather along the associated cold front across much of the northeast throughout the day. This same cold front extended southwestward and was approaching the Commonwealth throughout the overnight and morning hours on Wednesday. Storms that developed along the front surged into eastern KY, creating an outflow boundary. It is along this boundary that rain showers continued to set up, bringing persistent rounds of rain to portions of the state. In addition, Tropical Depression Nicholas was moving onshore along the Gulf Coast near the TX and LA border, pumping a decent amount of low level moisture northward and into the Commonwealth. So not only was rain persistent, but it was efficient, resulting in high rainfall rates and amounts. The combination naturally resulted excessive rainfall, and reports of flash flooding, especially in Bath County, where highest rates, amounts, and longevity all combined together.
episodes.163551: A large waterspout developed in association with a convective rain shower southwest of Key West.  The Florida Keys were in a col region between low pressure over the Bahamas and the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Nicholas over the northwestern Gulf states, with a daily record precipitable water value of 2.52 inches observed earlier in the morning from the Key West radiosonde data.
episodes.163761: Weak upslope flow coupled with a slow moving cold front and a weak mid-level disturbance triggered storm development. But moisture was limited in the lower levels. With storms that did develop, they were aided by modest lapse rates of around 8C/km with MLCAPE values up to 1000 J/kg. There was sufficient vertical shear and buoyancy to produce up to golf ball sized hail.

Water levels remain elevated with some properties still to be assessed and some streets and highways still impassable.
